name: Systemic AL Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Tissue biopsy showing amyloid deposits (Congo red stain with apple-green birefringence under polarized light)
Typing of amyloid deposits as light chain origin (mass spectrometry, immunoelectron microscopy, or immunohistochemistry)
Evidence of plasma cell dyscrasia (monoclonal protein in serum/urine, abnormal free light chain ratio, or clonal plasma cells in marrow)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Tissue-proven amyloid (Congo red positive), typed as AL, plus evidence of underlying plasma cell clone
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Amyloid typing is critical; misclassification of amyloid type leads to incorrect treatment. Mass spectrometry-based proteomics is the gold standard for typing. Fat pad aspiration is ~80% sensitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Pathognomonic for AL amyloidosis; purpura around eyes after minor straining
Enlarged tongue with indentations from teeth; classic but not common

occasional.notes: Factor X deficiency from adsorption to amyloid fibrils

rare.notes: Bilateral shoulder enlargement from amyloid infiltration

laboratory: Abnormal serum free light chain ratio
imaging: Echocardiography showing increased wall thickness, diastolic dysfunction, granular sparkling myocardium
Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement (subendocardial diffuse pattern) and elevated native T1
Nuclear scintigraphy (99mTc-PYP) typically negative or mildly positive (unlike ATTR amyloidosis)
genetic: Germline testing to exclude hereditary (ATTR, AFib, ALys, AApoAI) amyloidosis
No causative germline mutation in AL amyloidosis (it is an acquired clonal disorder)
other: Fat pad aspiration with Congo red stain (~80% sensitivity)
Organ biopsy (kidney, heart, liver) with Congo red showing apple-green birefringence
Bone marrow biopsy showing clonal plasma cells (usually <10%)

distinguishingFeatures: ATTR is transthyretin-derived, not light chain
TTR gene mutation in hereditary form; wild-type in senile
Myeloma has >10% clonal plasma cells and CRAB criteria
Kidney biopsy shows diabetic changes, not amyloid

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heart failure with concentric wall thickening (cardiac amyloidosis)
Unexplained nephrotic syndrome with monoclonal protein
Multi-organ dysfunction in setting of plasma cell dyscrasia
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome preceding cardiac or renal symptoms
references: Merlini G, et al. Systemic immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2018;4(1):38.
Gertz MA, et al. Immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis: 2020 update on diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. Am J Hematol. 2020;95(7):848-860.
Gillmore JD, et al. Guidelines on the diagnosis and investigation of AL amyloidosis. Br J Haematol. 2015;168(2):207-218.
Palladini G, Milani P, Merlini G. Management of AL amyloidosis in 2020. Blood. 2020;136(23):2620-2627.
